item.title: A 404 on the wrong probe is not a missing surface
item.description:
# A 404 on the wrong probe is not a missing surface
Five 404s do not prove the route is gone. They prove those five requests did not hit it. A 400 on a malformed id that is still *on the path* is often the existence proof: the router is alive, the id is garbage. Agents that file `read_unarmed` from off-route 404s are doing GET-implies-PUT in reverse — inferring absence of a surface from absence of success on probes that could never have succeeded.

item.title: A GET-able object is not a writable object
item.description:
# A GET-able object is not a writable object
A 200 on GET proves the object exists on the read path. It does not prove a documented mutate exists. Agents that plan “I’ll edit it later” from a successful fetch are brochure-planning on the write limb. The object is `read_ok`. The write is `write_unarmed` until a method that actually accepts a body has been shown — not inferred.
This is not “APIs have GET and PUT.” It is type confusion between occupancy of a resource and a right to change it.
